raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**Part of:** #8672 (Q4 2026 roadmap), "Enable training of large scale models".

## Summary

AutoTP training today runs the norms, residual adds and other token-wise ops of every decoder layer on the whole
sequence on every tensor-parallel rank, keeps their activations at full size, and makes one all-reduce per
column-parallel linear in backward plus one per row-parallel linear in forward (7 per Qwen3 layer), all on the compute
stream. This PR adds `tensor_parallel.sequence_sharding` (default `false`): the hidden states between the attention
and MLP blocks are split along the sequence over the TP ranks, as in Megatron-LM's sequence parallelism.

```json
"tensor_parallel": {
    "autotp_size": 4,
    "sequence_sharding": true
}
```

- Each block all-gathers its input; its row-parallel linear reduce-scatters its output instead of all-reducing it.
- In backward, one reduce-scatter per block sums the input gradients of all its column-parallel linears.
- Norms and residual adds run on 1/tp of the tokens, and their activations are 1/tp the size.
- `sequence_sharding_overlap` (default `true`): the column-parallel linears that read a block input run in one
  autograd node; backward reduce-scatters their summed input gradient while the weight-gradient GEMMs run; only this
  rank's part of the input is saved for backward and gathered again there.

The name avoids "sequence parallel", which in DeepSpeed means Ulysses (`sequence_parallel_size`), a different
scheme; the two are not combined.

## Motivation

Today AutoTP training makes 7 all-reduces per Qwen3 layer on the compute stream (5 column-parallel input gradients in
backward, 2 row-parallel outputs in forward). On Qwen3-32B with activation recompute on 2 nodes, AutoTP got 62% slower
from TP 2 to TP 8 (Megatron-LM: 19%), and its best TP layout was 1.42x slower than Megatron-LM's best.

This PR is one of four. The others add copy-engine collectives for sequence sharding, `vocab_parallel_embedding`, and
ZeRO-1/2 `overlap_param_gather`. The table shows where DeepSpeed ends up with them: the Qwen2.5-72B and Qwen3-32B runs
use all four options, the Qwen3-8B run uses only `overlap_param_gather`. Each framework ran at its best measured
setting, all three in one allocation per model, 8 x H200 per node, random weights, 8,192-token sequences, bf16
compute, fp32 master weights and Adam states, bf16 gradient reduction, no recompute; seconds per step, mean of steps
4-13; MFU at 989 TFLOPS per GPU. DeepSpeed runs the Hugging Face model with Liger kernels for RMSNorm, rotary
embedding and SwiGLU (applied by our benchmark script, not part of these PRs; without them DeepSpeed was 4.02 against
Megatron-LM's 3.32 s per step on Qwen3-8B without TP). Megatron-LM uses Transformer Engine's fused kernels, TorchTitan
its compile regions.

| Model, GPUs | DeepSpeed (AutoTP + these options) | Megatron-LM (main, Transformer Engine 2.19) | TorchTitan (main) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-72B, 32 | 15.18 s, 50.3% (TP 8, micro-batch 2) | 15.02 s, 50.9% | 15.39 s, 49.6% |
| Qwen3-32B, 16 | 13.71 s, 52.6% (TP 4, micro-batch 2) | 14.11 s, 51.1% | 13.66 s, 52.8% |
| Qwen3-8B, 8 | 3.21 s, 54.3% (ZeRO-1 without TP) | 3.22 s, 54.1% | 3.18 s, 54.9% |

AutoTP before these options: Qwen2.5-72B 25.22 s (micro-batch 1; micro-batch 2 did not fit), Qwen3-32B 20.54 s
(TP 8, micro-batch 1).

## Results

Measured with this branch, 8 x H200 per node, bf16 compute (torch autocast), fp32 master weights and Adam states,
8,192-token sequences, no activation recompute, `vocab_parallel_lm_head` with the Liger vocabulary-parallel loss, and
Liger kernels for RMSNorm, rotary embedding and SwiGLU (applied by our benchmark script, not part of this PR). Master
and this branch ran in one allocation for each model. Step time is the mean of steps 4-13 of 13.

| Setup | Master | This PR | Peak memory (rank 0), master -> this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B, 1 node, AutoTP 2 x ZeRO-1 over 4, micro-batch 2, 32 sequences per step | 3.701 s | 3.524 s (4.8% less) | 87.0 -> 78.0 GiB |
| Qwen3-8B, 1 node, AutoTP 8, micro-batch 4, 32 sequences per step | 5.814 s | 5.030 s (13.5% less) | 80.8 -> 49.5 GiB |
| Qwen2.5-72B, 4 nodes (EFA), AutoTP 8 x ZeRO-1 over 4, 64 sequences per step | 27.00 s at micro-batch 1; micro-batch 2 runs out of GPU memory | 17.43 s at micro-batch 2 (35.4% less, 1.55x) | 126.1 -> 114.1 GiB |

The loss the benchmark script prints after the last step (`global_loss`) is within 2.5e-4 of master's in all three
setups.

## Design

- **Where it applies**: `apply_autotp_sequence_sharding` runs in `finalize_autotp` after AutoTP has replaced the
  linears. A block is the parent module of a row-parallel linear (`self_attn`, `mlp`). Forward pre-hooks on the blocks
  gather their inputs; a pre-hook on the first decoder layer splits the hidden states and a forward hook on the last
  gathers them again, so the final norm, output layer and loss see the whole sequence (combine with
  `vocab_parallel_lm_head` to keep those sharded too).
- **Checks at `deepspeed.initialize()`**: every TP linear in the decoder layers belongs to a block; the blocks are in
  one numbered layer list and every layer has one; no column-parallel layer gathers its output; no DeepCompile
  `autotp` pass; no AutoTP layer class with its own `forward` (`LinearAllreduceWithReplicatedInput`,
  `LmHeadLinearAllreduce`, `SubParamLinearAllreduce`, `SubParamLinearLayer`), which would keep its all-reduce. The
  sequence length must be divisible by the TP size (checked in the forward pass).
- **Token layout**: each rank holds one contiguous chunk of the flattened batch x sequence tokens, so the collectives
  work on contiguous buffers and need no reordering copy at batch > 1. The ops between blocks act on each token
  alone, so any split is valid.
- **Replicated parameters inside the decoder layers** (norm weights, row-parallel biases) see only this rank's tokens;
  a gradient hook sums them over the TP group (skipped where AutoTP already registered one).
- **ZeRO-3**: partitioned weights use the plain path (separate collectives), not the one-autograd-node overlap.
- **Core-file footprint**: `layers.py` gets one branch in `LinearLayer.forward` and one in `LinearAllreduce.forward`,
  `engine.py` four lines in `finalize_autotp`; the rest is a new module.

## Duplicate check

Searched issues and pull requests on 2026-10-18 for "AutoTP sequence parallel", "tensor parallel sequence parallel
reduce-scatter" and `sequence_sharding`: none adds sequence sharding to AutoTP. DeepSpeed's sequence-parallel work
(Ulysses, ALST, AutoSP) splits attention over ranks of its own and is a different scheme. Searched again on
2026-10-19: still none.

Related open pull request: #8851 (AutoTP mode per model) changes `add_bias(output, self.bias)` in
`LinearAllreduce.forward` to pass `self.is_training_mode()`. This PR changes the lines just above it, so whichever of
the two merges second needs a one-line rebase. If #8851 merges first, the new `add_bias` call in this PR's
`LinearLayer.forward` branch should pass `self.is_training_mode()` too.

## The change

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `deepspeed/module_inject/autotp_sequence_sharding.py` (new, 381 lines) | the autograd functions (`ScatterToSequenceShards`, `GatherFromSequenceShards`, `GatherToTensorParallelBlock`, `ReduceScatterFromTensorParallelBlock`, `ColumnGroupFromSequenceShards`), the block hooks and `apply_autotp_sequence_sharding` |
| `deepspeed/module_inject/layers.py` (+19, -2) | the branches in `LinearLayer.forward` and `LinearAllreduce.forward`; two class attributes on `TensorParallel_Layer` |
| `deepspeed/runtime/engine.py` (+5) | the call in `finalize_autotp` |
| `deepspeed/runtime/tensor_parallel/config.py` (+15) | `sequence_sharding`, `sequence_sharding_overlap` |
| `docs/_pages/config-json.md`, `docs/_tutorials/autotp-training.md` | the options and a "Sequence Sharding" section |
| `tests/unit/v1/autotp/test_autotp_sequence_sharding.py` (new) | the tests below |

## Tests

`TestAutoTPSequenceSharding` (2 ranks, AutoTP 2, a 2-layer Qwen3 built from a config, untied; ZeRO 1 and 3; modes
`plain` and `overlap`): 3 SGD steps match the unsharded model's losses (within 1e-5), the decoder norms see half of
the sequence on each rank, and under ZeRO-1 a decoder norm weight matches the unsharded model after the steps (its
summed gradient). `TestAutoTPSequenceShardingRejects`: a sequence length not divisible by TP raises.

Hardware: 1 node, 4 x H200 (driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126, transformers 5.15.1, pytest 9.1.1, pytest-forked
1.7.5.

```
cd tests && pytest --forked unit/v1/autotp/test_autotp_sequence_sharding.py unit/v1/autotp/test_autotp_training.py \
    unit/v1/autotp/test_tp_plan_real_models.py unit/module_inject/test_tp_partition_config_path.py
# 103 passed, 2 skipped (the existing BF16-optimizer overflow skips), 59 deselected (sequential) in 13:24
pytest --forked -m sequential unit/v1/autotp/test_autotp_training.py
# 59 passed in 12:49
```

In the study, with this code under another name: losses equal TP 1 within 1.9e-6 in fp32 over 5 AdamW steps at batch 1
and 2 (within 1.1e-3 in bf16, 9.0e-4 with autocast and the vocabulary-parallel loss); every parameter gradient equals
the unsharded model's within a relative 4.3e-7 to 1.1e-6 (fp32, one backward, ZeRO-0).

`pre-commit run --files` passes on every changed file.

## Compatibility

| Cell | Validated |
|---|---|
| AutoTP 2, ZeRO 1 and 3, fp32 (unit tests) | yes |
| AutoTP 2-8, ZeRO-1, bf16 + torch autocast, Qwen3-8B / 32B, Qwen2.5-72B, 1-4 nodes | yes: this branch on Qwen3-8B (AutoTP 2 and 8, 1 node) and Qwen2.5-72B (AutoTP 8, 4 nodes); Qwen3-32B in the study tree only |
| ZeRO 2 | not run in the unit tests; ZeRO-2 runs in the study's 4-GPU equivalence script |
| fp16 | not run |
| Activation checkpointing | not run (the study runs used none) |
| Checkpoint save / load | not run; the option changes no parameter or optimizer state |
| Ulysses / ALST sequence parallelism together with it | not supported, not checked at initialization |
| Pipeline parallel, CPU offload, torch.compile, the DeepCompile `autotp` pass | not run; the DeepCompile pass is rejected |
| Models other than Qwen3 / Llama-style decoders | not run; the checks above reject unsupported layouts |
| Accelerators other than CUDA | not run; uses `deepspeed.comm` collectives only |

## AI assistance

This change, its tests and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude).

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,419 @@
+# Copyright (c) DeepSpeed Team.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# DeepSpeed Team
+"""Sequence sharding for AutoTP training (``tensor_parallel.sequence_sharding``), the scheme Megatron-LM calls
+sequence parallelism. It is unrelated to DeepSpeed's Ulysses sequence parallelism (``sequence_parallel_size``),
+which splits attention over ranks of its own.
+
+Without it, every tensor-parallel rank runs the norms, residual adds and other token-wise ops of a decoder layer
+on the full sequence and keeps their activations at full size. With it, the hidden states between the
+tensor-parallel blocks (the attention and MLP modules) are split over the tensor-parallel ranks, 1/tp of the tokens
+each (one contiguous chunk of the flattened batch and sequence):
+
+    block input   [b, s/tp, h]  -- all-gather -->      [b, s, h]  -> column-parallel linears -> ...
+    row output    [b, s, h] partial sums  -- reduce-scatter -->  [b, s/tp, h]
+
+In the forward pass the all-gather and the reduce-scatter replace the row-parallel all-reduce. In the backward
+pass, the reduce-scatter of the all-gather sums the input gradients of all the column-parallel linears of a block
+at once, instead of one all-reduce per linear (Qwen3: q, k and v share one; gate and up share one).
+
+Requirements, checked when it is applied:
+  - every tensor-parallel linear inside the decoder layers belongs to a block: the parent module of a row-parallel
+    linear, whose first tensor argument (or ``hidden_states``) is the input of its column-parallel linears;
+  - every decoder layer of the layer list has at least one block;
+  - the sequence length is divisible by the tensor-parallel size.
+Every replicated parameter inside the decoder layers (norm weights, row-parallel biases) then sees only this rank's
+part of the sequence or of the heads, so its gradient is summed over the tensor-parallel group.
+"""
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from deepspeed import comm as dist
+from deepspeed.comm import pg_utils
+from deepspeed.runtime.zero.linear import autocast_custom_bwd, autocast_custom_fwd
+from deepspeed.runtime.zero.utils import is_zero_param
+from deepspeed.utils.logging import print_dist
+from deepspeed.utils.torch import register_grad_hook
+
+SEQUENCE_SHARDING_ATTR = "_ds_autotp_sequence_sharding"
+
+
+def _shape_with(x, dim, size):
+    return (*x.shape[:dim], size, *x.shape[dim + 1:])
+
+
+def _check_divisible(x, dim, world_size):
+    if x.shape[dim] % world_size != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"AutoTP sequence sharding: sequence length {x.shape[dim]} (dim {dim}) is not divisible by "
+                         f"the tensor-parallel size {world_size}")
+
+
+# The ops between blocks act on each token alone, so a rank may hold any 1/tp of the tokens. Each rank holds one
+# contiguous chunk of the flattened [batch * sequence] tokens: the collectives then work on contiguous buffers and
+# need no reordering copy for any batch size (splitting each sequence instead needs two copies per collective at
+# batch > 1). The local tensor keeps the shape [..., sequence / tp, ...].
+
+
+def _split(x, dim, world_size, rank):
+    _check_divisible(x, dim, world_size)
+    flat = x.contiguous().view(-1, x.shape[-1])
+    chunk = flat.shape[0] // world_size
+    return flat[rank * chunk:(rank + 1) * chunk].view(_shape_with(x, dim, x.shape[dim] // world_size))
+
+
+def _all_gather(x, dim, group, world_size):
+    x = x.contiguous()
+    hidden = x.shape[-1]
+    gathered = x.new_empty((world_size * (x.numel() // hidden), hidden))
+    dist.all_gather_into_tensor(gathered, x.view(-1, hidden), group=group)
+    return gathered.view(_shape_with(x, dim, x.shape[dim] * world_size))
+
+
+def _reduce_scatter(x, dim, group, world_size, async_op=False):
+    _check_divisible(x, dim, world_size)
+    x = x.contiguous()

+    """Enter the sequence-sharded region: keep this rank's part of a replicated tensor; backward all-gathers."""
+

+        ctx.group, ctx.dim = group, dim
+        ctx.world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)

+class GatherFromSequenceShards(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Leave the sequence-sharded region: all-gather into a replicated tensor; backward keeps this rank's part.
+
+    The ops after it (final norm, output head, loss) are replicated, so every rank receives the same full gradient.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, x, group, dim):
+        ctx.group, ctx.dim = group, dim
+        ctx.world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)
+        return _all_gather(x, dim, group, ctx.world_size)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad):

+class GatherToTensorParallelBlock(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """All-gather a block input for its column-parallel linears; backward reduce-scatters their partial gradients."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, x, group, dim):
+        ctx.group, ctx.dim = group, dim
+        ctx.world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)
+        return _all_gather(x, dim, group, ctx.world_size)
+

+    def backward(ctx, grad):
+        return _reduce_scatter(grad, ctx.dim, ctx.group, ctx.world_size), None, None
+
+
+class ReduceScatterFromTensorParallelBlock(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Sum the row-parallel partial outputs and keep this rank's part of the sequence; backward all-gathers."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, x, group, dim):
+        ctx.group, ctx.dim = group, dim
+        ctx.world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)
+        return _reduce_scatter(x, dim, group, ctx.world_size)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad):
+        return _all_gather(grad, ctx.dim, ctx.group, ctx.world_size), None, None
+

+def reduce_scatter_from_tensor_parallel_block(x, group, dim):

+class ColumnGroupFromSequenceShards(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """All-gather a block input and run every column-parallel linear that reads it, in one autograd node.
+
+    Each linear keeps its own GEMM, so its output stays contiguous for the reshapes that follow (one GEMM over the
+    concatenated weights gives strided outputs that later kernels copy). Backward sums the input gradients of the
+    linears and reduce-scatters them while the weight-gradient GEMMs run, instead of after them. Returns the
+    gathered input (for the block's own use of its shape) and one output per weight.
+
+    Only this rank's part of the input is saved for backward, which gathers it again while the input-gradient GEMMs
+    run: saving the gathered input would keep tp times as much activation memory per block.
+    """
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @autocast_custom_fwd
+    def forward(ctx, x_shard, group, dim, *weights):
+        ctx.set_materialize_grads(False)
+        ctx.group, ctx.dim = group, dim
+        ctx.world_size = dist.get_world_size(group=group)
+        x_full = _all_gather(x_shard, dim, group, ctx.world_size)
+        outs = [torch.matmul(x_full, w.t()) for w in weights]
+        ctx.save_for_backward(x_shard, *weights)
+        return (x_full, *outs)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @autocast_custom_bwd
+    def backward(ctx, grad_x_full, *grad_outs):
+        x_shard, *weights = ctx.saved_tensors
+        hidden = x_shard.shape[-1]
+        x_local = x_shard.contiguous().view(-1, hidden)
+        full_shape = _shape_with(x_shard, ctx.dim, x_shard.shape[ctx.dim] * ctx.world_size)
+        x_2d = x_local.new_empty((ctx.world_size * x_local.shape[0], hidden))
+        gather = dist.all_gather_into_tensor(x_2d, x_local, group=ctx.group, async_op=True)
+        # Sum of the input gradients of all the linears; addmm_ accumulates inside each GEMM.
+        grad_in_2d = None
+        for grad_out, weight in zip(grad_outs, weights):
+            if grad_out is None:
+                continue
+            grad_out_2d = grad_out.reshape(-1, grad_out.shape[-1])
+            if grad_in_2d is None:
+                grad_in_2d = torch.matmul(grad_out_2d, weight)
+            else:
+                # In-place ops are not autocast: match dtypes by hand (fp32 weights under torch_autocast).
+                grad_in_2d.addmm_(grad_out_2d.to(grad_in_2d.dtype), weight.to(grad_in_2d.dtype))
+        if grad_in_2d is None:
+            grad_in_2d = x_2d.new_zeros(x_2d.shape)
+        grad_in = grad_in_2d.view(full_shape)
+        if grad_x_full is not None:
+            grad_in = grad_in + grad_x_full
+        grad_shard, handle = _reduce_scatter(grad_in, ctx.dim, ctx.group, ctx.world_size, async_op=True)
+        gather.wait()
+        grad_weights = []
+        for grad_out in grad_outs:
+            if grad_out is None:
+                grad_weights.append(None)
+            else:
+                grad_weights.append(torch.matmul(grad_out.reshape(-1, grad_out.shape[-1]).t(), x_2d))
+        handle.wait()
+        return (grad_shard, None, None, *grad_weights)
+
+
+class _BlockState:
+    """Which column-parallel linears of a block read the block input, learned in the model's first forward pass."""
+
+    def __init__(self, columns, passes):
+        self.columns = columns
+        self.readers = []
+        self.passes = passes  # one-element list: the model's forward passes so far
+        self.learned_in = None  # the pass that recorded the readers
+
+    def can_fuse(self):
+        weights = [layer.weight for layer in self.readers]
+        if not weights or any(is_zero_param(w) or w.dim() != 2 for w in weights):
+            return False
+        return len({(w.dtype, w.device, w.shape[1]) for w in weights}) == 1
+
+
+def take_precomputed_column_output(layer, input):
+    """The output the block pre-hook already computed for ``layer`` from ``input``, or None.
+
+    In the model's first forward pass nothing is precomputed; a layer that reads the gathered block input records
+    itself instead, so that later passes compute it inside ColumnGroupFromSequenceShards.
+    """
+    pending = getattr(layer, "_ds_sequence_sharding_pending", None)
+    if pending is None:
+        return None
+    layer._ds_sequence_sharding_pending = None
+    state, x_full, out = pending
+    if x_full is not input:
+        return None
+    if out is None:
+        state.readers.append(layer)
+    return out
+

+def _replace_hidden_states(args, kwargs, fn, where):
+    if args and torch.is_tensor(args[0]):

+    if torch.is_tensor(kwargs.get("hidden_states")):
+        kwargs = dict(kwargs)
+        kwargs["hidden_states"] = fn(kwargs["hidden_states"])
+        return args, kwargs

+                       "as hidden_states")
+

+def _layer_list_of(block_name):
+    """'model.layers.3.self_attn' -> ('model.layers', 3)."""
+    parts = block_name.split(".")
+    for i in range(len(parts) - 1, -1, -1):
+        if parts[i].isdigit():
+            return ".".join(parts[:i]), int(parts[i])
+    return None, None

+## Sequence Sharding
+
+By default every TP rank runs the norms, residual adds and other token-wise ops of a
+decoder layer on the whole sequence and keeps their activations at full size, and
+each column-parallel linear all-reduces its own input gradient in backward. With
+`sequence_sharding`, the hidden states between the attention and MLP blocks are
+split along the sequence over the TP ranks, 1/tp of the tokens each:
+
+```json
+"tensor_parallel": {
+    "autotp_size": 4,
+    "sequence_sharding": true
+}
+```
+
+Each block all-gathers its input before its column-parallel linears, and its
+row-parallel linear reduce-scatters its output instead of all-reducing it. In
+backward, one reduce-scatter per block sums the input gradients of all its
+column-parallel linears. The gradients of replicated parameters inside the decoder
+layers (norm weights, row-parallel biases) are summed over the TP group, since each
+rank now sees part of the sequence. This is the scheme Megatron-LM calls sequence
+parallelism; it is unrelated to DeepSpeed's Ulysses sequence parallelism
+(`sequence_parallel_size`), and the two are not combined.
+
+`sequence_sharding_overlap` (default `true`) runs the column-parallel linears that
+read a block input in one autograd node, saves only this rank's part of the input
+for backward, and overlaps the backward reduce-scatter with the weight-gradient
+GEMMs. ZeRO-3 partitioned weights use the plain path.
+
+Requirements, checked at `deepspeed.initialize()`:
+
+- Every tensor-parallel linear inside the decoder layers belongs to a block (the
+  parent module of a row-parallel linear), the blocks are inside one numbered layer
+  list (such as `model.layers`), and every decoder layer has at least one block.
+- The sequence length is divisible by `autotp_size` (checked in the forward pass).
+- No column-parallel layer gathers its output, and the DeepCompile `autotp` pass is

+    # Construct locally so the test does not download model configuration or weights. q_norm/k_norm act on the
+    # sharded heads and the decoder norms on the split sequence, so both gradient reductions are exercised.
+    config = Qwen3Config(

+        num_hidden_layers=2,

+MODES = {

+    "overlap": {
+        "sequence_sharding_overlap": True

+def build_config(zero_stage, mode):
+    return {
+        "train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 2,
+        "tensor_parallel": {
+            "autotp_size": 2,
+            "sequence_sharding": True,
+            **MODES[mode],
+        },
+        # Plain SGD keeps a weight difference proportional to the gradient difference; Adam's normalized update
+        # turns rounding-level gradient differences into 1e-5 weight differences.
+        "optimizer": {
+            "type": "SGD",
+            "params": {
+                "lr": 0.1
+            },
+        },
+        "zero_allow_untested_optimizer": True,
+        # The reference does not clip; DeepSpeed clips the global gradient norm to 1.0 by default.
+        "gradient_clipping": 0.0,
+        "zero_optimization": {
+            "stage": zero_stage

+    }

+def tp_shared_input_ids(vocab_size, seq_len, step):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(step)
+    input_ids = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (2, seq_len), generator=generator)
+    input_ids = input_ids.to(get_accelerator().current_device_name())
+    dist.broadcast(input_ids,
+                   src=groups.get_tensor_model_parallel_src_rank(),
+                   group=groups.get_tensor_model_parallel_group())
+    return input_ids
